claim.quote: A blind analysis of nuclear recoil events with energies between 3.3 keV and 60.5 keV finds no significant excess. This leads to a minimum upper limit on the spin-independent WIMP-nucleon cross section of 2.58 × 10−47 cm2 for a WIMP mass of 28 GeV/c2 at 90 % confidence level.

name: First Dark Matter Search with Nuclear Recoils from the XENONnT Experiment

summary.plain: XENONnT reported its first search for dark-matter (WIMP) nuclear recoils. A blind analysis of about 1.1 tonne-years of data found no significant excess and set an upper limit on the spin-independent WIMP-nucleon cross section of 2.58 × 10⁻⁴⁷ cm² for a 28 GeV/c² WIMP at 90% confidence level, improving on XENON1T for the same exposure.
summary.technical: About 1.1 tonne-year exposure, 5.9 t sensitive liquid-xenon mass; intrinsic 85Kr and 222Rn concentrations reduced to unprecedentedly low levels, giving an electronic-recoil background of (15.8 ± 1.3) events/(t·y·keV) in the region of interest. A blind analysis of nuclear recoils between 3.3 and 60.5 keV finds no significant excess: minimum upper limit on the spin-independent WIMP-nucleon cross section 2.58 × 10⁻⁴⁷ cm² at 28 GeV/c² (90% CL). Spin-dependent limits are also provided; limit and sensitivity improve on XENON1T for the same exposure.

title: First Dark Matter Search with Nuclear Recoils from the XENONnT Experiment
why_it_matters: The abstract says the intrinsic 85Kr and 222Rn concentrations in the liquid target were reduced to unprecedentedly low levels, giving an electronic-recoil background of (15.8 ± 1.3) events/(t·y·keV), and that both the limit and the sensitivity improve on previous XENON1T results for the same exposure.
